content:
The image shows a corn stalk base with:
- Severe rotting at the lower stalk/crown area
- Dark brown to black discoloration of the outer stalk tissue
- Wet, slimy, macerated appearance of the affected tissue
- The rot is concentrated at the base/crown region near the soil line
- Surrounding leaves are dried/dead
- The decay appears soft and mushy (water-soaked), not dry
- No visible fungal structures or smut masses

This pattern of wet, dark, foul-smelling-looking rot at the stalk base near the soil line is characteristic of **Bacterial Stalk Rot** (*Erwinia* spp.). The soft, water-soaked, dark brown discoloration at the crown with macerated tissue is the hallmark symptom. It differs from fungal stalk rots (Charcoal, Diplodia, Gibberella) which tend to show internal pith discoloration with fungal signs rather than this external wet rot at the very base.
